entities.evidence: Genesis 11:20 identifies Serug as Reu’s son. Here he fathers Nahor.
Serug fathers this Nahor, who becomes Terah’s father in Genesis 11:24. The Nahor named in Genesis 11:26 is Terah’s son.

analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and an apocopated verb form.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for Serug. The proposed derivation from שׂרג and the gloss “mutterer” lack support in this verse.
draft.evidence: Genesis 11:20 names Serug in the phrase וַיּוֹלֶד אֶת שְׂרוּג, “and he fathered Serug.”

analysis.evidence: Genesis 11:20 names Serug as Reu’s son. Here Serug lives thirty years and fathers Nahor, whose name follows the direct-object marker אֶת.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix. It is the subject of both וַיְחִי and וַיּוֹלֶד, each a third-person masculine singular verb.

analysis.evidence: שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה gives Serug’s age in years. He lived thirty years before he fathered Nahor.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute common noun with no prefix or suffix. The singular follows the numeral שְׁלֹשִׁים, “thirty.”
Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ and no suffix

analysis.evidence: In וַיּוֹלֶד אֶת נָחוֹר, “he fathered Nahor,” אֶת marks the personal name נָחוֹר as the definite direct object of וַיּוֹלֶד.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

evidence.note: Serug lived two hundred years after he fathered Nahor.

article.name: נָחוֹר
article.summary: In Genesis 11:23, Nahor is the son of Serug. The meaning of the name is uncertain.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נָחוֹר and leave its root unassigned.
draft.definition: Nahor, the personal name borne here by Serug’s son.
draft.evidence: Genesis 11:23 names Nahor as the child whom Serug fathered.

analysis.evidence: Serug is the subject of וַיּוֹלֶד (“he fathered”), and אֶת marks נָחוֹר as its direct object. The verse identifies Nahor as Serug’s son.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal proper noun with no prefix or suffix. The direct-object marker אֶת is a separate word.
